text: {"question":"How does the helium‑abundance measurement from LBT, which breaks the geometric degeneracy in varying‑electron‑mass cosmologies, interact with deuterium‑to‑hydrogen ratio constraints from BBN when assessing the viability of such models?","reference_answer":"The LBT helium measurement narrows the allowed shift in the electron mass, thereby tightening the range of matter density and Hubble constant values that can satisfy the CMB data. When deuterium‑to‑hydrogen ratio limits from BBN are added, the models that would otherwise accommodate a larger electron‑mass shift become disfavoured, because the higher baryon‑density values preferred by the electron‑mass variation are in conflict with the precise deuterium abundance measurements. Thus, the combined LBT and BBN constraints significantly reduce the parameter space for varying‑electron‑mass scenarios."}
